author: evac
description: Server activity analytics: tracks when chat is busy and when it's quiet (human messages only, counts never content). Hour-of-day averages, daily/weekly/monthly reports, a weekday x hour heatmap, a best-window finder for events, anomaly flags, per-channel ranking, member joins/leaves, new-member retention (who leaves fast, who talks, who sticks; joins by invite source like Disboard vs discord.me; past joins rebuilt from the join/leave log), a self-updating live board, weekly and monthly digests in the mod channel, a resumable history backfill, and a JSON export for analysis. Mods only, mod channel only.
install_msg: Thanks for installing serverpulse! Everything lives under `.pulse` (alias `.activity`) and works for mods in the mod channel only. Tracking starts at the next full hour; run `.pulse backfill 30` to import the last 30 days so reports work right away. Defaults: mod channel and mod role are pre-set, the two bot channels are ignored, and weekly (Mon 9am) + monthly (1st, 9am) digests post to the mod channel. Try `.pulse`, `.pulse week`, `.pulse hours`, `.pulse hour 8pm`, `.pulse heatmap`, `.pulse best`, `.pulse board start`, `.pulse export`.
short: Server activity analytics: busy/quiet hours, daily/weekly/monthly reports, heatmap, live board, digests.
name: serverpulse
end_user_data_statement: This cog stores hourly message counts per channel (no message content) and, for 90 days, a per-user daily message count keyed by user ID, used for the mods-only top-chatters view. For new-member retention it stores one record per join: user ID, join/leave time, the invite used, account age, whether they finished onboarding, and the days they posted in their first 45 days (no content). Data lives in the bot's data folder and is not shared externally; a user's per-user counts and join records are deleted on a Red data-deletion request.
